description:
Propose bed layouts inside a plot. Writes nothing.

Reads the plot's outline and returns `variants` layouts, each with its
metrics (beds, path share, worst and median compactness, narrowest path,
and for rows the row-metres, turns and headland share), warnings, a small
SVG preview, and `accept.blocks`: the exact list to pass to
goodearth_block_save(blocks=…) to keep it. Blocks already inside the plot
are retired under a `v1 ` name in that same list, so the old layout stays
readable and its names are free. The new beds are saved in a group named
for the plot, inside each group the plot is in. A layout over 100 blocks comes as
`accept.batches`, saved in order.

Paths are the space between beds, kept at the width asked for after the
edges are softened. Below one terrain cell (about 90 m) neighbouring beds
share a climate sample; the warning says so, because the beds are then
bookkeeping and the climate answers stay at the plot's scale.

bearing.description: Rows: degrees clockwise from north the rows run along.

bearing_rule.description: Rows, when no bearing: "longest_axis" (fewest turns) or "east_west" (even light).

block.description: The ground to answer for: a block you have saved — its id, its name, one of its aliases, or any part of its name that only one block has (e.g. "Meadow" for "Lower Meadow"). If several match, the error lists them with their ids. Blocks may overlap; each answers for its own ground. Save one with block_save first; geometry travels once, not on every call.

compactness_min.description: The Polsby-Popper floor a bed must meet, 0.2–0.9.

headland_m.description: Rows: turning room clear at both ends, 0–30 m.

min_row_length_m.description: Rows: shorter fragments are dropped, 1–200 m.

npub.description: Required. Your Nostr public key (npub1...) for credit billing.

paths.description: Path widths in metres: {perimeter, room, bed}. Defaults 3.0, 3.0 and 1.8 for organic; rows default to a 0.6 m path between rows.

seed.description: The same seed gives the same layout.

size_mix.description: Organic: relative bed sizes dealt across the beds, e.g. [1, 1, 2].

style.description: "organic" (rooms of irregular beds) or "commercial_rows" (parallel beds on a bearing).
